name: OPRO: Large Language Models as Optimizers
description: OPRO (Optimization by PROmpting) is an evaluation framework that uses LLMs as meta-optimizers: the model iteratively proposes and refines solutions based on a natural-language description of the optimization problem and the history of previous candidates with their scores. Benchmark tasks include linear regression, Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) instances, and prompt optimization evaluated on GSM8K and Big-Bench Hard (BBH) tasks. Performance is measured by how close the LLM-generated solutions come to known optima.
typical_sota_score: Prompt optimization with OPRO on GSM8K: ~80–83% accuracy with PaLM 2-L; BBH: ~51–54% depending on task set.
reputation: Influential Google DeepMind paper (2023) that established LLM-as-optimizer as a research paradigm; widely cited in prompt engineering and optimization literature.
notes: The framework does not constitute a fixed benchmark dataset but rather an evaluation methodology applied to existing benchmarks (GSM8K, BBH) and small optimization instances. TSP experiments use synthetic instances only. Reproducibility depends heavily on the backbone LLM used.
